title: The Expansion Pack
logline: Lily's father Mickey shows up with Thirty-Somethings, a board game about the gang, and Lily isn't in the box: she's the sealed expansion pack, sold separately. Lily forbids anyone to play it, so naturally everyone gets hooked behind her back, Marshall sinks his Bigfoot fund into it, and the envelope only Lily can open turns out to hold forty-three cards' worth of proof that her father was listening the whole time.
coldOpen: Aunt Lily's dad, Mickey Aldrin, invented a hundred and fourteen board games.

couch.line: There was Foreclosure, fun for the whole family. There was Jury Duty, which took six weeks to play.
There was Bedbugs, which did not come with bedbugs. Most copies.
You two have played exactly one of them. The one with the sandwich. Both halves.

guests.name: Deb Fogarty
guests.role: Owner of Fogarty's, the corner store near the apartment. Keeps one shelf of board games between the batteries and the cat food, and still has all twelve copies of the last game Mickey sold her. Unimpressed in a low, slow monotone.

facts.lily.dad_game: Mickey's game Thirty-Somethings is about the gang; never sold, one copy
facts.lily.game_piece: Lily and Marshall are two halves of one sandwich; Mickey has no piece
facts.ted.game_piece: Ted is a tiny blue French horn in Mickey's game
facts.robin.game_piece: Robin is a beaver in Mickey's game: Canadian, builds walls
facts.barney.game_piece: Barney is a little suit; suiting up advances two spaces
facts.lily.first_painting: Sold to a dentist in Queens, secretly bought back in 2007
facts.lily.dad: Still angry at Mickey; invited him to Thursday game night at eight
facts.marshall.bigfoot_fund: Gone: all $412 went to Mickey for printing
facts.lily.eighth_birthday: Mickey missed it for a Dayton toy fair; gift was a game called Tetanus

opens.note: Mickey is invited to Thursday game night at eight but has no piece in the game yet. Whether he keeps showing up on time is open.
Mickey owes Marshall $412, the entire Bigfoot fund.

scenes.summary: Mickey arrives with Thirty-Somethings. Everyone gets a piece; Marshall's is half a sandwich. Lily isn't in the box: she's the expansion pack, sold separately. She walks out. Mickey leaves her sealed envelope with Marshall.

beats.line: Mickey Aldrin only ever showed up with two things: a new game, and a need for money.
Mickey!
Dad.
Forty years in the business, and I finally made a game about something I know.
Owing people money?
It's called Thirty-Somethings. It used to be Twenty-Somethings, but it took me a while.
Ted, you're a tiny blue French horn.
Mickey. That's beautiful.
The horn was always too much.
Robin, you're a beaver. Canadian. Builds walls.
Because I'm Canadian, right?
Sure.
Barney, you're a little suit. Every time you suit up, advance two spaces.
I have never respected a man in flannel until this moment.
Marshall. You're half a sandwich.
Why only half?
That's in the expansion pack.
I don't understand it, and I love it.
And where am I?
You're the expansion pack. Sold separately.
Of course I am.
Her piece. It's sealed. She's the only one who opens it.

scenes.label: Later
scenes.summary: Mickey's gone. Lily's case against him; her prediction of how Mickey will tap Marshall for money. Marshall promises nobody will play. He's holding the sealed envelope Mickey left.

beats.line: He missed my eighth birthday for a toy fair in Dayton. He brought me back a game called Tetanus.
In fairness, Tetanus had a really fun spinner.
Marshall.
He wasn't around for my life, and now he wants to sell my friends at a drugstore.
And I know exactly how this goes.
Marshall, buddy. I'm forty dollars short for the printer.
Mickey. Say no more.
That's offensive. I would never.
You'd do it in a heartbeat.
Two heartbeats. Minimum. I'm a lawyer.
Promise me nobody plays that game.
I promise. Nobody plays.
And throw that envelope out.
Absolutely.

scenes.summary: Hard cut: the whole gang minus Lily mid-game in the booth. Marshall's loophole, Ted's Lecture square, the half sandwich that never leaves start, and Barney's theory that the expansion always holds the overpowered piece.

beats.line: Barney suits up. Advance two spaces.
That's five times tonight. You're cheating.
The deck knows what it wants.
Should we feel bad about this? You promised Lily.
I promised nobody would play. I'm not playing. I'm the banker.
Lawyered. Oh, God, I lawyered my wife. Who needs change for a fifty?
The Lecture. Ted explains where a word comes from. Everyone else loses a turn.
That is a gross mischaracterization.
Mischaracterization, actually, from the Greek for a stamping tool—
And we lose a turn.
Your half sandwich hasn't left the start square in three games.
He's not slow. He's waiting for someone.
Speaking of. Let's talk about that envelope.
Basic game design. The expansion always has the overpowered piece. Whoever's in there is unstoppable.
It's Lily.
Exactly.
The beaver wins again.
MacLaren's is directly under the apartment. I've redrawn the board. To scale.
Barney! Put Lily down!
One more game.
Shh! She's asleep! Whose turn is it?

scenes.summary: Lily's prediction was wrong: Marshall offers his whole Bigfoot fund before Mickey can ask. Deb at Fogarty's needs five pieces, not four. Mickey describes the fifth. Lily walks in for glue sticks.

beats.line: Lily's prediction turned out to be wrong about one thing.
Marshall, buddy, I'm a little—
Four hundred and twelve dollars. My entire Bigfoot fund.
I was going to say nervous.
Mickey Aldrin. I still have all twelve copies of Hostage.
Deb, Hostage was ahead of its time.
It came with a real ski mask. A man wore it in here to rob me.
Ma'am, this one's different. It's about real people. I'm the half sandwich.
Five friends, four pieces. People see that, they think somebody died.
The fifth is in the expansion. Only she can open it.
What's she like?
Five-three. Red hair. Can stop a grown man with one look.
Deb, do you have glue sticks? I need forty.
Marshall?
That's the expansion pack.

scenes.summary: Lily and Marshall come home to find Ted, Robin and Barney mid-game. The whole secret comes out. Lily's real wound: he doesn't get to be good at them. She hits Marshall where it hurts and walks out without opening the envelope.

beats.line: Barney suits up! Advance two spaces!
It's not what it looks like.
It looks like you're a beaver.
Four hundred and twelve dollars, Marshall?
It was the Bigfoot fund.
You have a Bigfoot fund?
Had. I diversified.
How long?
Three weeks. Tuesdays, Thursdays, and one Sunday we don't talk about.
Forty-one games. I've never won. The beaver is a monster.
In our defense, it's a really good game. The economy is shockingly elegant.
I know it's good! That's the problem!
He doesn't get to be good at us.
Lilypad, if you'd just open the envel—
You love him because your dad showed up for everything. You think they all do.
Play all you want. I'm not opening it.

scenes.summary: Robin finds Lily alone at the bar. The beaver thing: Mickey nailed Robin after meeting her twice, which means he has Lily down cold. Open it.

beats.line: He made me a beaver.
He's a hack.
He said I build walls. So I spent a whole weekend proving him wrong. Alone. With the door locked.
He's met you twice.
Twice, and he nailed me. So he's got you down cold. That's what's scaring you.
I'm not scared. I'm furious. I've been furious since 1987. It's very organized.
So open it. If it's garbage, you get to stay furious.
And if it isn't?
Then you're a beaver too.
I hate that game.
It's so good.

scenes.summary: Lily has opened the envelope. Mickey comes for the box. The cards: the painting she sold to a dentist and secretly bought back, a thing she told only him. He writes her down after every call. It is moving, and it is not enough: he's never seen her classroom. She invites him to Thursday. He's said he'd be there before.

beats.line: Marshall said I could pick up the box. Deb passed. She thought somebody died.
Sit down, Dad.
You sell your first painting to a dentist in Queens. Then you buy it back. Lose two hundred dollars.
Nobody knows that. Marshall thinks it's hanging over a spit sink in Queens.
You called me from his waiting room. My birthday, 2007.
I asked you if I was crazy.
I said no. I've got six hundred copies of my own games in a garage. Wrong guy to ask.
Lily keeps a secret for almost an hour. Advance one space.
That's slander.
It's one space, honey. I was generous.
We talk twice a year.
Four minutes each. I write it all down after you hang up.
You wrote me down.
It's the only job I ever kept.
You knew about a dentist in Queens, Dad. You've never seen my classroom.
I know.
Thursday. We play at eight.
I'll be there.
You've said that before.

scenes.label: Thursday, 7:58 PM
scenes.summary: Game night. Barney reports Mickey has been in the hallway since 7:15. Mickey knocks at eight. Lily's piece is the other half of Marshall's sandwich. Her rules are wildly overpowered: Barney was right. Mickey has no piece; he's sold separately. Lily goes first and draws a card Mickey wrote years ago.

beats.line: Lily, your dad's in the hallway, staring at his watch like it owes him money.
How long has he been out there?
No idea. I've only been watching him since seven-fifteen.
At eight o'clock exactly, Mickey knocked.
My piece. It's the other half of the sandwich.
Lilypad. We're a whole sandwich.
Lily always goes first. Lily can't go backward. Lily collects double on her birthday.
This is the most overpowered piece in the history of board games!
She's my daughter.
You lost to a beaver forty-one times. Sit down.
So which piece is Mickey?
He's not in the base game. He's sold separately.
That's fair.
Your dad shows up on time. Advance one space.
One space.
